guard_streams.write_limit: Checker predictions and availability categories are indicative network-level information. They cannot independently establish live orderability, exact corrected r2 coverage or measured speed for a selected parcel.

facts.detail: The coverage-checker information page was last updated on 25 June 2025.
The mobile and broadband checkers accept a postcode.
The mobile checker presents coverage by provider.
The broadband checker reports standard, superfast and ultrafast service availability.
Results can be viewed as interactive maps.
The checker can be viewed in Welsh.
Ofcom links separate mobile and broadband checker FAQs.
Fixed-broadband and mobile data are available to developers through APIs.
The checker cannot report maintenance or current network incidents.
The page signposts the broadband USO where download speed below 10 Mbit/s may qualify.

guard_streams.source: Mobile coverage checker frequently asked questions
guard_streams.write_limit: Mobile coverage predictions, sampled verification and postal-district performance cannot be transferred to fixed-broadband parcel serviceability or parcel-measured speed.

facts.detail: The checker compares the four main UK mobile network operators.
Ofcom uses Ordnance Survey data to identify UK properties.
Property-address data is updated in the checker three times a year.
Ofcom provides an API based on the same mobile coverage data used by the checker.
Coverage is based on operator computer-model predictions of mobile signal propagation.
The prediction models consider obstructions including hills, trees and buildings.
Ofcom verifies predictions through real-world tests using dedicated measurement hardware at sample locations.
Tests indicate predictions are generally reliable but cannot guarantee coverage at every location.
Ofcom aims to refresh coverage information every three months or with Connected Nations publications.
Very local factors can cause real experience to differ from area-average predictions.

guard_streams.source: About the Ofcom mobile and broadband checker
guard_streams.write_limit: Predicted speeds and network submissions can be incomplete or differ from operational availability. They cannot be treated as exact selected-parcel orderability or a measured speed.

facts.detail: Predicted broadband speeds are supplied by leading UK broadband networks.
No prediction for an address does not necessarily mean broadband is unavailable.
Ofcom advises checking network websites where no checker prediction is shown.
Ofcom aims to collect coverage information from all fixed-network providers.
Some providers, particularly smaller networks, may not yet be included.
In-building network performance can reduce received speed.
The number of devices using online services can affect speed.
Line length, age and repair condition can affect performance.
A network provider may sell directly or through service-provider resellers.
Property access, maintenance or upgrades can make a listed service operationally unavailable.
